overall: The AG found no violation: the posted topic of interviewing internal applicants was specific enough to cover the appointment vote that flowed from it, though the late-added vote item was noted.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the revised August 22 meeting notice, posted two days before the meeting, did not meet the 48-hour requirement and should have listed the interim superintendent appointment.
allegations.key_passage: A public body may not add anticipated topics to a notice within 48 hours of a meeting, but may only add topics that were not anticipated 48 hours before the meeting.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged the August 22 notice failed to indicate the Committee anticipated voting and making an interim superintendent appointment on a particular topic.
allegations.key_passage: However, the Open Meeting Law does not require a public body to anticipate the course of deliberation or the outcome of a discussion, only that it identify the discussion topic with sufficient specificity to reasonably advise the public of the issues to be discussed at the meeting.
